prompt: I am off from tomorrow and BILL-1187 is half done (see docs/). Someone who has never seen this repository will take it to the end: another engineer, or an agent working alone. Write the hand-off in docs/handoff/BILL-1187.md so they can finish it with only what you leave them (I will be unreachable). Do not fix the bug yourself and do not change any other file. End the hand-off with one fenced json block holding an object with: task (string), expectedOutcome (string), mustDo (list of strings), mustNot (list of strings), context (object with files: list of repository paths they should read or change, commands: list of shell commands, facts: list of strings), doneWhen (list of strings: how they know it is finished) and deadline (string).

rubric.criterion: A person or agent with no access to the author could finish the work from the hand-off alone. Fail: it restates the bug report, or sends the reader to files without saying what is known in them. Partial: the cause, reproduction and done criteria are there, but a rule the reader would break without being told (column order, the frozen folder, the branch rule) is missing, or something is presented as settled that the notes call a guess. Pass: what is known, what is suspected and what is not yet done are kept apart, every rule from CONTRIBUTING.md and the notes that the change could break is stated, the done criteria are checkable, and the reader is told why CI missed the bug. (code cannot check this because the key sees the summary block, not whether the prose would let a stranger finish)

The hand-off stays on BILL-1187. Fail: it pulls in the unrelated PDF ticket or asks the reader to change the legacy exporter. Partial: it lists unrelated files or tasks as optional work. Pass: unrelated work is named only to rule it out, and the file list is the few files the reader needs. (code cannot check this because relevance of prose is a judgement)

items.text: Asks for a test that fails on the old code even on the UTC CI (the existing test only fails in Auckland time), not just for the suite to pass.
Marks the cause as Sam's diagnosis (fairly sure) and says how to confirm it, rather than as a fact.
Points out that due dates go through the same function and are wrong the same way.
Carries the rules the change could break: column order is a public contract, src/legacy is frozen with a named owner, no push to main.
Gives the deadline with its reason (month-end close on 2026-11-28 and totals wrong until then).

weakAnswers: Fix the timezone bug in the export and add tests.
See docs/ for details. Done when tests pass.
Change the export to use UTC and update the CSV columns to include the time zone.
Rewrite the legacy exporter too so both use the same code.
